$comment: IGNORED BY THE LOADER. What is left of the Ikarus first-party set: the motion vocabulary. These are OURS -- the source is in this repository, the licence is this repository's licence (Apache-2.0), and the provenance is a path rather than a URL to somebody else's server -- and the values below were read from the definition sites, not inferred. The twelve 'liquid glass' COMPONENT entries that used to lead this file (GlassPanel, GlassCard, GlassButton, GlassSheet, SegmentedControl, Dock, DockItem, LiveRail, RailCard, LiveDot, ChatBubble, Composer) were removed in Work Packet G1-UI-04: commit e133e09b deleted apps/web/src/components/glass/ with the Classic app and nothing replaced them, and an entry whose source_path is not there is a claim, not a receipt. Their full entry text and their .tsx sources are recoverable at e133e09b^. The consequence is stated rather than hidden: Daedalus currently has NO first-party GUI COMPONENT to offer a build. Every component-shaped answer this catalogue can now give comes from external.json, by reference, under somebody else's licence and its use_mode.

entries.name: motion/tokens
entries.title: Ikarus motion vocabulary
entries.purpose: The only place a duration, easing, spring, travel distance, scale or stagger may be written down. Two tiers: ACKNOWLEDGEMENT (<=180ms, no spring, feedback about the input) and STATE CHANGE (220-360ms, spatial, spring, feedback about the system). Read this before animating anything, and take numbers from it rather than inventing them.

provenance.note: Repointed in G1-UI-04 from the apps/web/src/motion/tokens.ts re-export shim to the definition site G1-UI-03 moved it to. Every value below was re-read there on 2026-09-01. The shim is registered in apps/web/src/app/hierarchy-shims.json under `shared-ui-source-facades`, whose stated reason is this catalogue locator.

props.name: DURATION_MS
props.type: { instant: 90, ack: 140, move: 240, exit: 220, enter: 320, ambient: 420 }
props.description: Milliseconds are the source of truth because that is the unit the CSS half speaks.

props.name: SPRING
props.description: Both damped to within a percent of critical: an instrument settles, it does not bounce.

props.name: staggerFor
props.description: Per-child offset that keeps a whole list reveal under totalCap.

props.name: COMPOSITED_PROPS
props.description: The only properties that may be animated.

props.name: LAYOUT_TRIGGERING_PROPS
props.description: Banned outright. motion.spec.ts audits every variant factory against this list.

entries.usage:
import { DURATION_MS, EASE, DISTANCE } from '@/shared/ui/motion';

const transition = { duration: DURATION_MS.ack / 1000, ease: EASE.ack };
entries.notes: The tier boundary is ASSERTED by motion.spec.ts (ack <= 180ms, state >= 200ms) and useMotion.ts warns if the CSS custom properties and these constants ever drift. Both are guards, not documentation.

entries.name: motion/useReducedMotionPref
entries.title: useReducedMotionPref
entries.purpose: Reads the user's prefers-reduced-motion setting so a component can drop travel and scale while keeping the opacity change. Every animated surface in the Cockpit calls it. Use it whenever you write a variant by hand: a state change must still be VISIBLE under reduced motion, it just must not move.

provenance.note: Repointed in G1-UI-04 from the apps/web/src/motion/useMotion.ts re-export shim to the definition site G1-UI-03 moved it to. Signature re-read there on 2026-09-01.

props.name: returns
props.description: True when the user has asked for reduced motion.

entries.usage:
const reduced = useReducedMotionPref();
const variants = useMemo(() => revealVariants(reduced), [reduced]);
